taglines: Friday. You made it. You're not sure how. The forensics on this week would not hold up in court. But you're here and that's what matters and please stop asking follow-up questions.
Someone just sent a Slack message that says 'quick question' and then went silent. That was eleven minutes ago. The question is not quick. Nothing that starts this way ever is.
The standup ran forty-five minutes. Nothing was unblocked. The blockers are now blocking the original blockers. We have achieved a blocking recursion. Engineering is thriving.
You read an article this morning that said the key to productivity is a consistent morning routine. You read it at 9:47 AM in bed with yesterday's cold coffee. Bold of it to assume.
It is Friday and someone just filed a critical bug that requires 'eyes on it today.' The person with the context left at 4:30 PM yesterday. They are in a different time zone. Godspeed.
Your to-do list has seventeen items. You will complete two of them today. They will be the easiest two. The other fifteen will roll to Monday where they will be joined by nine new friends.
The deploy is going out this afternoon. Someone is already composing the incident post-mortem in their head. Call it preparation. Call it experience. Call it knowing your people.
Friday afternoon energy: technically present, spiritually on a dock somewhere, laptop open but eyes soft, one AirPod in, one foot already in the weekend. Nobody can prove otherwise.
